subject: acorn ant
title: A Tapeworm Makes Ants Live Like Queens, So a Woodpecker Can Eat Them

scenes.text: This parasite makes ants live longer. It's not a gift.
Workers of this tiny ant rarely live past two years.
But workers with tapeworm larvae turn pale yellow, stop working, and get pampered by their sisters, even more than the queen.
After three years, over half were alive. Fewer than one in twenty healthy workers were.
The catch: that tapeworm can only grow up inside a woodpecker.
A slow, pampered ant is easy prey. The longer it lives, the longer it waits to be eaten.

description:
Temnothorax nylanderi workers infected with the tapeworm Anomotaenia brevis turn yellowish, become less active and get more care from nestmates.
After three years more than half of infected workers were still alive, while over 95% of uninfected ones had died. The tapeworm needs a woodpecker to eat the ant to finish its life cycle.
Would you take a longer life if this was the price?
first_comment: One ant can carry up to 70 tapeworm larvae, and its queen can live up to 20 years. What other parasite is this sneaky?
